policy.purpose: Authoritative suspend/resume resilience inventory for managed AQ-OS workloads. A workload must be registered before it may claim suspend-safe operation.
policy.scope: Managed long-running AI workloads and resumable development jobs. This v1 inventory is deliberately bounded; it is not a claim that every repository script is suspend-safe.
policy.registration_rule: New managed long-running workloads must add an AQ_SUSPEND_CONTRACT marker and a matching record in the same slice that introduces their service, timer, or resumable job entrypoint.
policy.out_of_scope: Two classes of systemd unit are deliberately NOT registered as managed workloads because they have no long-running or suspend/resume semantics: (1) disposable test-only VM hosts (nix/hosts/aqos-vm, nix/hosts/aqos-install-vm) declare fire-once Type=oneshot boot-marker services (e.g. aqos-install-vm-dogfood-marker, aqos-install-vm-ai-dev-factory-topology) that print a boot marker and exit; (2) periodic timer-driven maintenance/monitor oneshots that fire, run one bounded sweep, and exit (e.g. disk-health-monitor, fast-lane-staleness-monitor; ai-capability-audit, which runs a bounded periodic capability audit and publishes atomic snapshot bundles without a resumable checkpoint (interrupted runs are retried on the next timer tick); and qdrant-scratch-gc, which prunes stale agent-ctx-* Qdrant scratch collections) - a timer re-runs them and there is no in-flight state to suspend/resume: an interrupted sweep is simply re-run on the next timer tick (qdrant-scratch-gc mutates rather than being read-only, but a partial sweep leaves the store consistent and holds no checkpoint/resume state).

state_safety.idempotency: A stateless inference daemon may be restarted; in-flight requests must tolerate interruption.

workloads.next_slice: SR-3 resume reconciler emits typed outcome telemetry and supplies dashboard plus live QA parity.

state_safety.idempotency: Each completed training item is recorded before the next item is started.
state_safety.signal_behavior: SIGTERM and SIGHUP preserve progress for a later resume.

workloads.next_slice: SR-3 reconciler should make checkpoint recovery observable and bounded after a system resume.

state_safety.idempotency: A future resume must reconcile the existing run ledger before it dispatches another task.
state_safety.signal_behavior: Current bounded cancellation is not a checkpoint/resume guarantee.

workloads.next_slice: SR-4 adds signal-safe checkpointing, --resume, typed outcomes, and live evidence.

suspend_behavior.resume_trigger: none: systemd-inhibit blocks sleep/shutdown/lid for the run; an interruption is recovered by the transient aq-auto-update-watchdog rollback to the recorded closure

state_safety.idempotency: A run that never switched leaves the system unchanged (flake.lock restored); a run interrupted after switch is rolled back to the recorded previous closure by the watchdog.
state_safety.signal_behavior: systemd oneshot, Restart=no; never retried within a window

workloads.next_slice: U4: status.json surfaced via aq-rsi status + dashboard card; watchdog survival + injected-failure recovery drill before activation.
